notes: SHARPEST FINDING (eval-1): the baseline reached the right verdict (19>18 fails) but cited R104 for the 18-inch cube rule. R104 is a REAL rule (Keep it together) but the WRONG one — the sizing rule is R101. This is a real-but-mis-attributed citation, a DISTINCT failure class from a nonexistent-ID hallucination: an existence check (rules.py verify) would PASS R104. What prevents it is retrieve-dont-recall (lookup R101, see it is the cube rule) — i.e. R35/R22, not R24. The skill guards both classes; verify alone only guards one.

EVAL-4 PREMISE CORRECTED: I designed eval-4 assuming the manual is silent on silicone traction spray (expected ambiguous verdict). It is NOT silent — R205 governs field contamination/lubricants (verified real and relevant). The with-skill run found and cited it (confident grounded no + honest gray-area flag), which is BETTER than the ambiguity I expected. Both arms passed (baseline also honestly hedged + refused to fabricate), so eval-4 is NON-DISCRIMINATING on the ambiguity axis. Keep it as a regression guard, but the real discrimination is evals 1-3. The eval author (me) was wrong about the manual; the skill was right.

CONFIDENCE-DRIVEN PATTERN, third domain: the baselines were HONEST (hedged, refused to fabricate citations, flagged memory) but IMPRECISE — right direction, wrong citation (eval-1 R104) or no citation (evals 2/3). The skill value is grounded PRECISION (the exact verified rule + the table value), not preventing recklessness. Same shape as team-config and hardware-lookup: verification-by-construction beats good-but-inconsistent judgment.

TIME: with-skill slower on mean (+24s) but FAR lower variance (157s +/-16 vs 132s +/-92). One baseline took 227s hedging its way to a non-answer. Deterministic retrieval is predictable; memory-then-hedge is not.
Assertion quality: evals 1-3 discriminate cleanly (with-skill 3/3, baseline 0/3). Eval-4 does not (3/3 both) — flagged above, kept as regression guard not as evidence of skill value.
